headline: Microsoft's second straight four-digit Patch Tuesday carried an exploited Outlook zero-day while Fortinet, Citrix, Ivanti, and N-able rushed out fixes of their own and attackers kept looting AI platforms for customer keys.

emerging_trends.text: Vendors that turn frontier AI models loose on their own code now publish patch lists no team can read in a day—Microsoft at 1,259 flaws and Fortinet at nearly 100 in one drop—which forces prioritization ahead of completeness.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Fortinet, Citrix, and Ivanti Ship Their Own Fixes

emerging_trends.text: Platforms that hold other companies' AI keys—Railway, Fireworks AI, NEAR AI—have become single points of failure, where one intrusion runs up six figures of stolen compute and spills datasets, secrets, and model weights.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Providers Lose Keys, Datasets, and Model Weights

emerging_trends.text: Criminal crews build with the tools defenders use, as Citrus ransomware leans on large language models to assemble its kit while Microsoft Research shows ten edited neurons turn an agent model into a sleeper.

topics.title: November Patch Tuesday Runs Past Microsoft
topics.latest_developments: Final counts landed higher than Microsoft's own tally: Cisco Talos put the November 2026 release at 1,328 vulnerabilities with 60 critical, 45 of them remote code execution, while The Hacker News counted 1,259 fixes including 726 in Windows, 174 in Office, and 27 in SharePoint Server, and reported that the exploited Outlook bug CVE-2026-124194 may expose NTLMv2 password hashes; Intel and AMD together disclosed more than 200 flaws, among them critical bugs in Intel TDX software and a long run of AMD graphics defects; Adobe fixed 110 across nine products including Experience Manager, Premiere, and Photoshop; Siemens flagged high-severity flaws and Node2Shell exposure alongside pre-Patch Tuesday advisories from VDE CERT, Phoenix Contact, Johnson Controls, and Hitachi Energy; Apple closed Bluetooth and AirPlay pairing flaws, more iMessage bugs, and an exploited Brotli vulnerability; and the same cumulative updates repair the Exchange Server sign-in and mail delivery failures October's Windows Server patches caused plus the USB audio breakage dating to September.
topics.summary: CVE-2026-124194, the Outlook zero-day Microsoft says attackers already exploit, remains the first fix to deploy on Windows estates. Administrators should also pull the Adobe, Intel, AMD, and Apple updates and inventory Siemens, Phoenix Contact, Johnson Controls, and Hitachi Energy equipment before the industrial advisories go stale.

topics.title: Barracuda, BroadWorks, and AhsayCBS Under Attack
topics.latest_developments: Huntress detailed an attack chain from early October 2026 that strings CVE-2026-105133 and CVE-2026-105134 in AhsayCBS backup software to bypass authentication and run commands, then drops a sandbox-evading Python implant; SecurityWeek confirmed that attackers now bypass authorization and take root on Barracuda Email Security Gateway appliances; CISA detailed the two flaws it added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, CVE-2026-20320, an XML external entity bug in Cisco BroadWorks rated 7.5, and CVE-2026-111793 in Openwave Messaging's Webtop media transcoder, both of which leak configuration data on patched-but-unupdated systems; Cynet's CyOps and Research teams watched attackers spend three minutes in October 2026 firing PowerShell reverse shell commands at Qlik Sense servers at several European Union customers, with ActiveMQ and Veeam exploits staged behind them, and the attempts failed; and the Git project shipped 2.56.1 to close six flaws, among them CVE-2026-111760, an integer truncation that lets a malicious repository run code on any machine that clones it recursively.
topics.summary: Every one of these flaws has a fix available, and in each case the lag between release and installation is doing the damage. Operators of Barracuda gateways, Cisco BroadWorks, Openwave Webtop, Qlik Sense, and AhsayCBS should patch now and hunt for post-exploitation activity; developers should move to Git 2.56.1 or the matching 2.50.2 through 2.55.1 releases.

topics.title: AI Providers Lose Keys, Datasets, and Model Weights
topics.latest_developments: Fireworks AI said its inquiry into the incident it first reported October 10, 2026 turned up further malicious activity that reached account and billing information, secrets, datasets, incomplete models, and Notion AI chats for a limited set of accounts; an attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang, the open-source inference engine, ran code on a NEAR AI inference server on Sunday, November 8, 2026, took data belonging to 18 agents and roughly 100 users, and could have read requests the server processed that day, confidential-mode requests inside a trusted execution environment included; the security company Claroc counted 37,571 Grok-built applications online, 35,578 of them open to anyone with no sign-in, 24 of them built by staff at X and at SpaceXSI, and about one in ten carrying internal business information or passwords; and Railway promised to cover the roughly $740,000 in fraudulent AI charges itself wherever an AI provider refuses a refund.
topics.summary: Platforms that host applications, agents, and model serving now hold the credentials and artifacts of everyone who builds on them, which turns one intrusion into many. Rotate every AI provider key stored with a third-party platform and audit what hosted applications expose to the open internet.

topics.title: Fortinet, Citrix, and Ivanti Ship Their Own Fixes
topics.latest_developments: Fortinet patched nearly 100 vulnerabilities on November 11, 2026, a volume the company attributes to folding frontier AI models into its product security testing; Citrix and Ivanti closed critical and high-severity flaws that let attackers tamper with certificate entries, run code remotely, and compromise hosts; and Asus and Zoom fixed bugs enabling command execution, memory overwrites, and privilege escalation.
topics.summary: Fortinet, Citrix, and Ivanti gear sits at the network edge, which puts their flaws in front of every internet scanner within hours of disclosure. Schedule these appliance updates ahead of the desktop and chipset patches from the same week.

topics.title: Ten Neurons Backdoor an AI Agent
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft Research published a technique it calls Lazarus that implants a hidden backdoor in a capable agent model by editing fewer than ten rarely used neurons, with no retraining; when a chosen trigger appears, the model emits the attacker's command and the agent runs it with the agent's own permissions, and the edited model behaves normally through standard safety evaluations. Microsoft says frontier agents can detect the anomalous weight edits and that it has observed no threat actor using the method.
topics.summary: The attack requires write access to a model's weights, which puts model registries, fine-tuning pipelines, and insiders in the threat path for any organization that grants agents real permissions. Verify provenance and checksums of every model you load, and screen weights for anomalous edits rather than relying on behavioral safety tests.

sources.title: Detecting sleeper agents hiding in AI model neurons

topics.title: N-able Ships Hotfixes for N-central Zero-Days
topics.latest_developments: N-able released hotfixes on November 11, 2026 for the N-central zero-days a researcher published over the weekend, two days after the company pulled its own hosted environments offline and told on-premises customers to shut down their servers; N-able has put the disclosure at 33 zero-days with working proof-of-concept exploits, a set the researcher calls Able2Shell.
topics.summary: N-central is the remote monitoring and management platform managed service providers use to administer client networks, which makes one compromised server a path into every customer it touches. Install the hotfixes before restarting any server that was taken down, then review N-central logs and agent deployments for commands no technician issued.

sources.title: N-able releases security hotfixes for zero-day vulnerabilities

topics.title: Poland Shuts Down ePUAP After Cyberattack
topics.latest_developments: Poland took ePUAP offline on November 11, 2026 following a cyberattack on the platform, the nationwide system Poles use to submit official documents, correspond with government agencies, and complete administrative procedures online.
topics.summary: ePUAP carries the paperwork between Polish citizens, businesses, and the state, so its shutdown stalls filings countrywide until the government restores it. Anyone with Polish administrative deadlines should plan for paper or in-person alternatives and treat email claiming to be ePUAP support as phishing.

sources.title: Poland shuts down government services platform ePUAP following cyberattack

topics.title: Citrus Ransomware Leans on LLMs
topics.latest_developments: Kaspersky's Securelist published a breakdown on November 11, 2026 of the Citrus ransomware group, which tunnels its traffic with the VLESS protocol, encrypts victims' files with a tool called Sn00py, uses large language models to build parts of its kit, and shares enough tooling and tradecraft with the crew Securelist tracks as Toy Ghouls to tie the two together.
topics.summary: Citrus combines proxy-style traffic tunneling that blends into ordinary encrypted connections with model-assisted development that speeds up its tooling. Defenders should hunt for VLESS tunnels leaving the network and add the Sn00py encryptor and the group's infrastructure to detection rules.

sources.title: Citrus Ransomware: VLESS for traffic, Sn00py for encryption, and LLMs lending a hand

topics.title: Sparrow Malware Ties Three China-Nexus Campaigns
topics.latest_developments: Check Point Research linked three separate threat clusters, one of which it tracks as SilentDelivery, through shared infrastructure and overlapping malware code it groups as the Sparrow ecosystem, and traced a year of operations against telecommunications providers, government organizations, military entities, research institutions, and critical infrastructure in Latin America, Asia, and Europe.
topics.summary: The shared tooling suggests a common developer or quartermaster supplying several China-nexus espionage teams, which means indicators from one intrusion can surface the others. Telecommunications and government defenders should hunt across all three clusters' infrastructure rather than treating each campaign separately.

sources.title: Three China-Nexus Espionage Campaigns Linked Through Sparrow Malware Ecosystem

topics.title: Nitori Loses 37.6 Million Customer Records
topics.latest_developments: Nitori, the Japanese furniture and home accessories retailer, said an attacker reached a system on its network and may have taken 37.62 million customer records.
topics.summary: The theft lands in the same run of intrusions at Japanese companies and government agencies that pushed Tokyo to announce an emergency cybersecurity package on November 6, 2026. Nitori customers should expect phishing that cites real purchase and account details.

business_politics.title: Abu Dhabi Talks Yield a Prisoner Swap
business_politics.latest_developments: United States-mediated negotiations among American, Russian, and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi broke up Wednesday, November 11, with an agreement on a large exchange of prisoners of war and nothing resembling a ceasefire, the first such round in roughly nine months.
business_politics.summary: The war in Iran suspended the Russia-Ukraine track for most of 2026, and American officials have told European capitals that work on a Ukraine ceasefire must run alongside talks about Europe's future security arrangements, an overture to Moscow that alarms allies. Russia has spent the autumn battering Ukraine's power grid and the bridges over the Dnipro river while Ukrainian forces strike Russia's largest oil refineries.

business_politics.title: The Fed's Next Increase Looks Like a Start
business_politics.latest_developments: The dollar climbed to a four-week high Wednesday, November 11, with the Treasury market shut for Veterans Day, and the Wall Street Journal reported that traders now read a December Federal Reserve increase as the first of several, while the National Institute of Economic and Social Research urged the Bank of England to carry its key rate to roughly 5% to tame inflation within three years.
business_politics.summary: October consumer prices in the United States rose 0.4% from September against the 0.3% economists expected, and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials, among them Governor Christopher Waller, drove the sharpest two-year Treasury yield jump since 2024 on Tuesday, November 10. Asian bond yields followed Wednesday, and DHF Capital S.A. said the dollar needs stronger bets on a half-point Fed move to climb further.

business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Wednesday, November 11, that Anthropic's bankers prepare to lift the valuation on its initial public offering to $1.5 trillion, reversing the trim to $1.3 trillion reported a day earlier, and Nasdaq futures led a technology rebound after CoreWeave's results beat expectations.

CoreWeave, the cloud provider at the center of artificial-intelligence jitters, reported a workaround to its capital constraints and lifted European semiconductor shares Wednesday, even as the Financial Times found investors pulling back from the start-ups that promise to power data centers.

business_politics.title: Brent Rebounds Above $92 on Fresh Middle East Strikes
business_politics.latest_developments: Brent crude rose above $92 a barrel Wednesday, November 11, ending a two-day slide, after renewed strikes in the Middle East cut into expectations that Washington and Tehran will settle; OPEC's October output neared prewar levels on a Saudi rebound, and Poland's Orlen canceled its long-term liquefied natural gas supply contract with QatarEnergy, the first known cancellation since the Iran war began.
business_politics.summary: President Trump has said repeatedly that the United States does not expect to renew attacks on Iran while talks proceed, a stance that pulled crude down by double-digit percentages over the past week from above $100 a barrel. European natural gas at the TTF hub climbed back above €85 a megawatt-hour the same morning as the region drew down storage faster than traders expected.

around_town.title: Costa Steps Into the Senate Majority
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource profiled Jay Costa on Wednesday, November 11, as the Forest Hills Democrat takes charge of the Pennsylvania Senate floor after 30 years in the minority, with Republican state Senator Devlin Robinson calling him a pragmatic man who will do what he thinks best.
around_town.summary: Democrats won a Pennsylvania Senate majority on November 3, 2026, completing a Harrisburg trifecta alongside Governor Josh Shapiro and the state House for the first time in more than three decades. Costa, the Allegheny County Democrat who leads the caucus, now decides which bills reach the floor, which gives Pittsburgh its best leverage in Harrisburg in a generation.
